thread:
tanya: Heads-up — ran into a surprising cancellation bug in the Go SDK generator sample app. When an auth refresh/retry happens mid-stream the generator iterator keeps yielding chunks after the caller cancels the context.

lee: ugh, that sounds like the classic "retry loses context" problem. Can you paste a minimal repro?

tanya: trimmed repro:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, _ := client.Generators.Generate(ctx, req)
// background token refresher may rotate token
cancel()
for p := range stream.Chunks() {
  fmt.Println(p) // still prints for a few seconds after cancel
}
```

tanya: Observed sequence in logs: original request -> 401 -> refresh flow -> retry request -> streaming continues. ctx.Err() is non-nil on the original goroutine but the retry keeps going.

omar: Quick theory: the retry path constructs a new http.Request with http.NewRequest and doesn't attach the original req.Context(). That would make the retried request immune to cancellation.

lee: Confirmed — looking in runtime/retry.go: when we rebuild the request on 401 we do not call req = req.WithContext(origCtx). Also the transport wrapper swaps Authorization header in-place which complicates things.

omar: Two possible fixes: (A) short term: set WithContext(origCtx) on retried requests so cancel propagates; add a unit/integration test for stream cancel during auth delays. (B) long term: decouple token refresh from per-request goroutines — return a retriable error and let centralized retry orchestration handle refresh so we don't block request goroutines.

tanya: I'm inclined to land the quick WithContext fix + test and also add a small note in the generator README about the gotcha (and a small sample showing context.WithTimeout for interactive flows).

lee: agree. Also add a comment in the transport code warning not to perform synchronous refresh on the request goroutine. Might save someone from copy-pasting the anti-pattern.

omar: I'll add an integration test that spins up a fake auth server which delays the token endpoint for N seconds; the test cancels the client ctx immediately and asserts the stream loop exits promptly. That reproduces the leak deterministically.

ci-bot: buildkite: started pipeline #9234 for branch fix/attach-ctx-on-retry

tanya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/378 — includes: attach original ctx to retried requests, integration test for stream cancel vs auth delay, README blurb and a tiny sampleapp tweak showing context.WithTimeout usage.

lee: LGTM, left a couple of style nits. Test reliably fails on master and passes on the branch.

omar: One more follow-up: we should add a brief note to the devex onboarding doc under "networking & auth" describing preferred patterns for token rotation: prefer background refresher with a threadsafe token supplier and avoid blocking refresh in per-request code.

tanya: thanks — I'll add that in a follow-up PR. Merging once CI is green.

omar: nice catch and good tests, thanks! :thumbsup:
